title: General Compute raises $100 million Series A, countering the neocloud disaster narrative
slides: Can General Compute prove the neocloud skeptics wrong?
It just raised $100 million in Series A funding
But most neoclouds are burning cash and failing
Your cloud costs may drop if this model works
Test one workload: demand transparent pricing now
thread_text:
1. Neocloud skeptics silenced?

General Compute just raised $100M Series A while most neoclouds burn cash and fail. Is this the model that finally works?

2. The $100 million bet

Investors are backing General Compute to prove neoclouds can be viable. But the graveyard of failed neoclouds is full of similar promises.

3. Cash burn crisis

Most neoclouds are burning cash and failing. General Compute claims its model is different — but can it survive long enough to prove it?

4. Cloud costs could drop

If General Compute's model works, your cloud costs may drop. That's a big if, given the industry's track record.

5. Test one workload today

Take a single workload and demand transparent pricing from your cloud provider. If they can't give it, you know who's really burning cash.
